text:
lucy: Heads up — noticed the sample app's browser SDK starts reconnect storms on flaky mobile networks. Repro on a Pixel emulator with 3G profile.

ben: I can repro on a coworker's network. The client throws repeated "Unexpected end of JSON input" and then immediately reconnects. After 10s we have dozens of fast reconnects.

kai: Quick dump of a failing chunk: `data: {"msg":"ok"}

:

` — the polyfill sees an extra colon comment squeezed into the same TCP packet and passes `:
data...` into JSON.parse.

lucy: Also, our backoff reset logic is racy: when the parser throws we call eventSource.close() then re-open instantly without jitter, so transient parse errors cause thundering reconnects.

rachel: Node SDK uses streaming parser that tolerates leading `:` comments and treats blank `data` as noop. Browser polyfill differs. That's an SDK parity bug.

ben: Proposed short-term patch for browser polyfill: trim leading comment tokens and ignore empty data blocks before parse. Pseudocode: ```js
function onRawChunk(raw) {
  // split on double newline, process each event block
  raw.split(/?
?
/).forEach(block => {
    const lines = block.split(/?
/);
    const dataLines = lines.filter(l => l.startsWith('data:')).map(l => l.slice(5));
    const payload = dataLines.join('
').trim();
    if (!payload) return;
    safeJsonParse(payload);
  });
}
```

kai: We should also harden the reconnect logic: add exponential backoff with cap and random jitter, and only treat parse errors as transient if X consecutive good parse successes are seen.

lucy: Agreed. Add a metric `sdk.stream.parse_failures` and a derived alert for >50/min for a given org to avoid widespread reconnect storms.

rachel: For sample-app onboarding: add a debug flag `?stream_debug` that prints raw frames and a `?no_heartbeat` to disable server comments so folks can rule out heartbeat interactions quickly.

ci-bot: CI pipeline triggered for branch `devex/sse-polyfill-fix` (jobs: lint, unit, browser-e2e).

ben: Edge-case: some proxies replace `

` with `
` sequences -> ensure our split regex handles CRLF and CR-only gracefully. Also handle stray ﻿ BOM at start of chunk.

kai: Tests we need: 1) combined `:
` comment + `data:` in one chunk, 2) split `data:` across TCP packets (partial first line + rest later), 3) CRLF/CR/BOM variations, 4) simulated slow network to ensure backoff prevents storm.

lucy: Action items: 
• ben: PR browser polyfill changes + unit tests (owner)
• kai: implement backoff + jitter in reconnect logic and add e2e in sample-app (owner)
• rachel: update onboarding docs with debug flags and note about flaky mobile networks (owner)
• lucy: create alert for `sdk.stream.parse_failures` and add dashboard widget for streaming errors (owner)

ben: I'll try to ship a patch release 0.4.2-canary today if CI passes.

lucy: If you see this in prod, toggling `?no_heartbeat=1` on the sample app is a quick mitigation until client patch lands.

rachel: Also leaving a note: review runtime's response flush behavior; if server coalesces heartbeat + data into single write when under pressure, we should ensure it emits a final `

` boundary.
